sentences.text: The purpose of the meeting was to prepare for a hearing on 15 December and to review the local authority's letter.
The client, Kerry Dobson, attended the meeting.
The solicitor, Priya Mehta, attended the meeting.
The client described contact with Tyler as occurring on Tuesdays and Thursdays at the family centre on Mill Lane.
The client reported that Tyler keeps asking when he can come home.
A worker at the family centre stated the contact session was 'warm'.
The client reported that Tyler lost his front tooth.
The client reported that Tyler likes the foster carers and that they have a dog.
Tyler is still attending Ashgrove Primary.
The foster carers drive Tyler to school.
Tyler's teacher stated he is doing better with his reading.
The local authority's letter requested a hair-strand test and asked about drug use.
The client stated they had not used drugs since June.
The client attends a support group on Wednesdays.
The client disclosed that they used crack last weekend.
The client initially denied using crack, stating 'forget I said that', but later confirmed they did.
The client disclosed that they used heroin since 3 November.
The client stated they use heroin every day.
The client stated they smoke heroin (not inject) and the cost is about £40 a day.
The client stated they pay for heroin using their Universal Credit and by borrowing from their nan.
The client's nan believes the money borrowed is for gas.
The client stopped picking up their script about three weeks ago.
The client confirmed they are still living at the flat on Corporation Street.
The client stated rent is paid directly.
The client admitted they are behind on council tax.
The client stated their primary objective is for Tyler to come home.
The client asked if a positive hair-strand test would result in contact being stopped.
The solicitor advised that a positive hair test would likely show up the client's use of crack and heroin.
The solicitor advised that it is better for the client to inform the social worker before the test result if they are back in treatment, as this looks different to the court.
The solicitor stated that courts do not usually stop contact over a relapse alone if the client is turning up sober and engaging.
